facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a slowly growing tumor on the scalp
otherwise healthy with no significant medical history
8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa
Dermoscopic findings of scalp nodule
8-mm red nodule showing irregular red lacunae without septa and irregular linear vessels
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor extending to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
Structures covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
Periodic acid−Schiff (PAS) staining showed positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels were positive for CD-31, negative for D2-40 (podoplanin) and HHV-8
α-smooth muscle actin highlighted the pericytes in the papillae

concepts.why: The presence of a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels, intravascular branching papillary structures, and swollen endothelial cells with intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules supports this diagnosis.

The tumor's composition of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures and the presence of hyaline globules in endothelial cells are characteristic of Dabska tumor.
The dermoscopic findings of irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and the absence of septa are consistent with hobnail hemangioma.
The presence of a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor extending to the superficial subcutaneous tissue supports this diagnosis.
Although less likely, the presence of a vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intravascular branching papillary structures cannot rule out angiosarcoma without further evaluation.
The presence of a vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and the patient's age could suggest Kaposi's sarcoma, although the lack of other characteristic features makes it less likely.
The dermoscopic findings of irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels are consistent with hemangioma, although the presence of other features suggests a more specific diagnosis.
The presence of a rapidly growing vascular tumor with irregular vessels could suggest pyogenic granuloma, although the lack of other characteristic features makes it less likely.

rationales.F01: The patient's age and sex are non-specific and do not particularly point towards any of the listed conditions.
rationales.F04: The dermoscopic findings of irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa are highly suggestive of a vascular tumor, particularly Papillary Intralymphatic Angioendothelioma or Dabska Tumor.
rationales.F06: The dermoscopic description of an 8-mm red nodule showing irregular red lacunae without septa and irregular linear vessels is highly indicative of a specific type of vascular tumor.
rationales.F07: The histopathological description of a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor extending to the superficial subcutaneous tissue is consistent with several types of vascular tumors, including Papillary Intralymphatic Angioendothelioma and Dabska Tumor.
rationales.F11: The immunohistochemical profile, particularly the positivity for CD-31 and negativity for D2-40 (podoplanin) and HHV-8, helps to differentiate between various vascular tumors and points away from Angiosarcoma and Kaposi's Sarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Dabska Tumor is chosen due to its strong support from generation findings, including well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor, ectatic thin-walled vessels, and intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules, as well as positive CD-31 and negative D2-40 and HHV-8 staining, which aligns with the case evidence.
